title: Loudoun Water Reclaimed Water Program — Phase 65 Northern Virginia large-load delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Northern Virginia large-load delivery reporting pack. Loudoun Water describes its reclaimed-water program and the commercial service concept available within a defined utility system, providing a water-infrastructure rail for data-center cooling questions.
key_findings: The utility operates a reclaimed-water program for eligible non-potable uses.
Availability depends on the utility network, location, connection, project design, and service arrangements.
A program description does not establish that a named data center has secured or uses reclaimed water.
why_it_matters: Which records connect load forecasts, local land-use rules, utility decisions, transmission, environmental permits, water, service acceptance, and reliability? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The program shows that water-source and network evidence should be checked project by project rather than inferred from regional availability.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a water-service dependency to the Northern Virginia shelf.
Supports project-level checks of source, connection, allocation, and use.
Prevents a general sustainability program from becoming an unsupported operating claim.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The page does not identify a project-specific allocation or contract.
It does not establish delivered volume, cooling design, potable-water displacement, or operating use.
Network availability and connection feasibility require separate current records.
